title: Derived maps from a free module compute zeroth homology
statement: Let A be any ring, and D(A) the unbounded derived category of left A-modules (localization of cochain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]). Let A[0] be the free rank-one left A-module in degree zero. There are additive equivalences b_E:Hom_D(A)(A[0],E) ≃+ H^0(E), where H^0(E) is viewed as an additive group, natural in every derived morphism: b_E'(g≫f)=H^0(f)(b_E(g)) for f:E→E' and g:A[0]→E. No commutativity of A or boundedness of E is assumed.

source.place: Proposition perfect-proposition-compact-is-perfect (Tag 09M1), proof, first paragraph; structure-sheaf case

proof.text: For a projective object P and E≤-1, choose a strictly bounded-above representative of E. Mathlib DerivedCategory.from_singleFunctor_obj_eq_zero_of_projective makes every map P[0]→E zero. This is the proved private helper projective_single_to_negative_eq_zero.

Use the truncation triangle τ<0(E)→E→τ≥0(E). Maps from P[0] to its first object and to that object shifted by 1 vanish by the preceding helper. The exact Hom sequence therefore makes postcomposition E→τ≥0(E) bijective. The source-library homologyFunctor_map_bijective_of_isLE_of_isGE makes H^0 bijective on maps P[0]→τ≥0(E); H^0(E)→H^0(τ≥0(E)) is an isomorphism. Combining the two squares proves projective_single_homology_bijective.

Take P=A, which is projective. Turn the bijective additive map H^0 on morphisms into an additive equivalence. Precompose with the inverse of H^0(A[0])≅A and apply ModuleCat.homAddEquiv and LinearMap.ringLmapEquivSelf A ℤ to evaluate at 1. The resulting map is b_E(g)=(ε.inv≫H^0(g))(1). The functor composition law gives naturality immediately; the final Lean proof uses rw and rfl.

lean.statement:
theorem derivedFreeModule_hom_homology (A : Type u) [Ring A]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} A)] :
    let H := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0 ⋙
      forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} A) AddCommGrpCat
    ∃ e : ∀ E : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A),
      (((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj
        (ModuleCat.of A A)) ⟶ E) ≃+ H.obj E,
      ∀ (E E' : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (f : E ⟶ E')
        (g : (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj
          (ModuleCat.of A A) ⟶ E),
        e E' (g ≫ f) = H.map f (e E g)
